subject: Quantitative Aptitude
title: Percentage
content:
**Percentage** means 'per hundred'.

- Percentage = (Part / Whole) x 100
- Successive change: net % = x + y + xy/100
- Increase 20% then decrease 20% gives a **4% net decrease**
- Fraction shortcuts: 1/2 = 50%, 1/3 = 33.33%, 1/4 = 25%, 1/5 = 20%, 1/8 = 12.5%

*Exam tip:* Build any percentage from 10%, 5% and 1% of the number.

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
title: Profit and Loss
content:
**Profit and Loss**

- Profit = SP - CP, Loss = CP - SP
- Profit % = (Profit / CP) x 100
- SP = CP x (100 + P%)/100 and CP = SP x 100/(100 + P%)
- Discount = Marked price - SP, always calculated on the marked price
- Two successive discounts a% and b% = a + b - ab/100

*Exam tip:* Treat CP as 100 units; it makes every problem a simple ratio.

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
title: Simple and Compound Interest
content:
**Interest**

- Simple Interest SI = P x R x T / 100
- Compound Amount A = P (1 + R/100)^n
- CI = A - P
- For 2 years, CI - SI = P (R/100)^2
- Rule of 72: money doubles in about 72 / R years at compound interest

*Exam tip:* Bank exams love CI - SI for 2 and 3 years; memorise the formula.

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
title: Time and Work
content:
**Time and Work**

- Work = Rate x Time. If A finishes in n days, A's rate = 1/n per day
- Together: 1/a + 1/b = 1/t, so t = ab/(a + b)
- Man-days: M1 x D1 = M2 x D2
- Take total work as the LCM of the days for quick integer rates
- Pipes: inlet pipes add work, outlet pipes subtract it

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
title: Speed, Time and Distance
content:
**Speed, Distance, Time**

- Speed = Distance / Time
- km/h to m/s: multiply by 5/18; m/s to km/h: multiply by 18/5
- Average speed over equal distances = 2xy/(x + y)
- Train crossing a pole: time = length / speed; crossing a platform: (train + platform) / speed
- Boats: downstream = u + v, upstream = u - v

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
title: Ratio, Proportion and Averages
content:
**Ratio and Proportion**

- a:b = c:d means ad = bc
- To combine A:B and B:C, make the B values equal
- Average = Sum / Number of items
- Alligation: (cheaper : dearer) quantities = (dearer - mean) : (mean - cheaper)

subject: Reasoning
title: Number and Letter Series
content:
**Series questions**

Check these patterns in order:
1. Constant difference (arithmetic)
2. Constant ratio (geometric)
3. Increasing differences (2, 6, 12, 20 -> +4, +6, +8)
4. Squares, cubes, primes
5. Alternating two series

For letters, convert to positions (A=1 ... Z=26) and look at the gaps.

subject: Reasoning
title: Blood Relations
content:
**Blood relation problems**

- Draw a family tree: use + for male, - for female, = for marriage
- Mother's brother = maternal uncle, father's sister = paternal aunt
- 'Son of my mother's only son' = my nephew
- Work step by step from the person the statement is about

subject: Reasoning
title: Direction Sense
content:
**Direction Sense**

- Always draw a small compass and plot each move
- Turning right from North gives East, then South, then West (clockwise)
- Net displacement uses Pythagoras: sqrt(a^2 + b^2) for perpendicular moves
- Sun rises in the east, so at sunrise your shadow points west

subject: Reasoning
title: Syllogism
content:
**Syllogism**

- Draw Venn diagrams for every statement
- All A are B + All B are C => All A are C
- Some A are B + All B are C => Some A are C
- Two particular ('some') statements give no definite conclusion
- Conclusions must follow in **all** possible diagrams

subject: English
title: Tenses and Subject-Verb Agreement
content:
**Tenses**

- Simple present: habits and facts. Present perfect: past action with present result (has done)
- Past perfect (had done) marks the earlier of two past actions
- Use *since* for a point in time and *for* for a duration
- Each, every, either, neither take **singular** verbs
- A collective noun (team, committee) is usually singular

subject: Indian Polity
title: Preamble of the Constitution
content:
**The Preamble**

India is a **Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic**.

- It secures Justice, Liberty, Equality and Fraternity
- 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' were added by the 42nd Amendment (1976)
- In *Kesavananda Bharati* (1973) the Supreme Court held the Preamble is part of the Constitution

*Exam tip:* UPSC and TNPSC repeatedly ask which words were added and by which amendment.

subject: Indian Polity
title: Fundamental Rights and DPSP
content:
**Fundamental Rights (Part III, Articles 12-35)**

1. Right to Equality (14-18)
2. Right to Freedom (19-22)
3. Right against Exploitation (23-24)
4. Right to Freedom of Religion (25-28)
5. Cultural and Educational Rights (29-30)
6. Right to Constitutional Remedies (32)

**DPSP** are in Part IV (36-51) and are non-justiciable. **Fundamental Duties** are in Part IV-A (Article 51A), 11 in number.

subject: Indian Polity
title: Parliament and the President
content:
**Union Parliament** = President + Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha.

- Lok Sabha: up to 550 members, 5-year term
- Rajya Sabha: up to 250 members, permanent house, one-third retire every 2 years
- Money Bills originate only in the Lok Sabha
- President: minimum age 35, elected indirectly by an Electoral College of **elected** MPs and MLAs for 5 years

subject: History
title: Mauryan Empire
content:
**Mauryan Empire (c. 322-185 BCE)**

- Founded by **Chandragupta Maurya** with Chanakya (Kautilya), author of the *Arthashastra*
- Bindusara expanded it; **Ashoka** (268-232 BCE) fought the Kalinga War and embraced Buddhism
- Ashoka's edicts are in Brahmi and other scripts; the Lion Capital of Sarnath is India's national emblem

subject: History
title: Indian Freedom Struggle Timeline
content:
**Key milestones**

- 1857 Revolt; 1885 Indian National Congress founded
- 1905 Partition of Bengal; 1919 Jallianwala Bagh
- 1920 Non-Cooperation; 1930 Dandi March / Civil Disobedience
- 1942 Quit India ('Do or Die'); 1947 Independence

*Memory trick:* 19-20-30-42-47 gives the order of Gandhian movements.

subject: Geography
title: Rivers and Physical Features of India
content:
**Indian Geography essentials**

- Ganga is the longest river within India; Godavari is the longest peninsular river
- Himalayan rivers are perennial; peninsular rivers are seasonal and mostly flow east into the Bay of Bengal (Narmada and Tapi flow west)
- Anamudi (Kerala) is the highest peak of peninsular India; Nanda Devi is the highest wholly in India
- South-West Monsoon brings most of India's annual rainfall (June-September)
- Black soil suits cotton; alluvial soil suits wheat and rice

subject: Economy
title: GDP, Inflation, RBI and Monetary Policy
content:
**Economy basics**

- **GDP**: value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a year
- **Inflation**: sustained rise in the general price level, measured in India by CPI
- **RBI** sets monetary policy: repo rate (lends to banks), reverse repo (borrows from banks), CRR and SLR
- Higher repo rate usually reduces inflation but slows credit
- **Fiscal policy** = government taxation and spending (Union Budget); **GST** has applied since 1 July 2017

subject: General Science
title: Newton's Laws of Motion
content:
**Newton's Laws**

1. **Inertia:** a body remains at rest or in uniform motion unless a net force acts on it
2. **F = ma:** force equals mass times acceleration
3. **Action-Reaction:** every action has an equal and opposite reaction

SI unit of force: newton (N). Momentum p = mv.

subject: General Science
title: Photosynthesis
content:
**Photosynthesis**

6CO2 + 6H2O + light energy -> C6H12O6 + 6O2

- Occurs in **chloroplasts**, using chlorophyll to trap sunlight
- Light reaction in the grana; dark reaction (Calvin cycle) in the stroma
- Oxygen released comes from the splitting of water

subject: General Science
title: Elements and the Periodic Table
content:
**Atoms and elements**

- Atom = nucleus (protons + neutrons) with electrons around it
- Atomic number = number of protons
- Periodic table: 18 groups, 7 periods; elements in a group have similar properties
- Symbols from Latin names: Na (natrium), K (kalium), Fe (ferrum), Au (aurum), Ag (argentum)

subject: Computer Awareness
title: Computer Fundamentals
content:
**Computer fundamentals**

- CPU = ALU + Control Unit + registers; RAM is volatile, ROM is non-volatile
- 1 byte = 8 bits; 1 KB = 1024 bytes
- Hardware = physical parts; software = programs (system and application)
- HTTP/HTTPS carry web pages; an IP address identifies a device on a network

subject: Tamil Nadu
title: Thirukkural and Sangam Literature
content:
**Tamil literature**

- **Thirukkural** by Thiruvalluvar: 1330 couplets in 133 chapters, divided into Aram (virtue), Porul (wealth) and Inbam (love)
- Sangam literature includes Ettuthogai and Pathupattu
- Five great epics: Silappatikaram (Ilango Adigal), Manimekalai, Sivaka Sindamani, Valayapathi, Kundalakesi

subject: Tamil Nadu
title: Chola Dynasty
content:
**The Cholas**

- Vijayalaya founded the medieval Chola line at Thanjavur
- **Rajaraja I** (985-1014) built the Brihadisvara Temple, Thanjavur
- **Rajendra I** founded Gangaikonda Cholapuram and led a naval expedition to Southeast Asia
- Chola village administration is famous for the Uttaramerur inscriptions
